speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you describe exactly what the vertigo feels like—does the room spin around you, or do you feel like you are moving while the room stays still? Also, how long does each episode of dizziness last?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in the ear on the side of the dizziness? Also, were you turning over in bed or looking up when the episode started?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the spinning sensation stop completely when you lay still, or did it persist regardless of your head position? Also, did you notice any weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking during the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let's test the duration and triggers. If you slowly turn your head to the side that triggered the dizziness, does the spinning sensation return immediately and last for less than a minute, or does it persist longer? Also, do you experience any double vision, slurred speech, or difficulty walking?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text: To confirm the diagnosis, I need to see if this movement triggers the vertigo again. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike_Manoeuvre
